practices: Assessments evaluate core understanding across 4 Themes (A to D). Focus on standard level topics. Strict adherence to command terms: State, Outline, Describe, and Explain are the dominant cognitive targets. Paper 1 assesses data analysis; Paper 2 requires short-answer and extended responses addressing core science systems.

keyTopics: Water structure, cohesive/adhesive properties, hydrogen bonding
Nucleic acid structures, RNA and DNA nucleotides
Cell theory, cell structure, eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells
Diversity of organisms, classification systems, cladistics
Structure and function of carbohydrates and lipids
Structure and function of proteins, peptide bonds
Enzymes and metabolism, active site, factors affecting rates

antiPatterns: Avoid HL extension topics under all circumstances. Never ask questions about: origins of cells (A2.1), lateral gene transfer (A3.2), active membrane pumps or detailed vesicle pathways (B2.1), sliding filament muscle theory (B3.3), detailed oxidative phosphorylation biochem (C1.2), light-independent reactions/Calvin cycle details (C1.3), complex chemical signaling receptors (C2.1), transcription regulation/operons (D1.3), linkage/dihybrid crosses/polygenic inheritance (D2.2). Keep questions conceptual, simple, and strictly aligned with standard level core.
